clue.text: A lackadaisical worker made to move smartly

definitions.meaning: to scamp work is to do it carelessly, so one who scamps is a slapdash worker
to scurry or dash about briskly

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who skimps on a job; the other is a quick, scurrying run.

clue.text: Doubt that carries little weight?

definitions.meaning: a moral hesitation about whether something is right
an old apothecaries' weight of twenty grains, very small

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a qualm of conscience; the other is a tiny unit of apothecaries' weight.

clue.text: The person wanting endless fruit one cannot provide

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the fruit word is dropped

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
I is the Roman numeral for one
cannot contracts to can't

explanation.surface: A hopeful person asks for fruit that someone else is unable to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provide' is a link word; I CANT runs on from APPL.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant is someone seeking a job or place, so one who wants something.

clue.text: The great fear of all in charge

parts.note: pan- is the Greek prefix meaning all

explanation.surface: The overwhelming dread felt by everyone in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming terror, a strong form of fear.

clue.text: Welcome no receipt being required

indicators.note: read as re-quired, worked over again, these letters are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A friendly greeting where nobody asks for proof of purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being required' rearranges NO RECEIPT; the printed line-break 're-quired' hints at the reworking.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is the way guests are greeted, so a welcome.

clue.text: One has to pay out around the United States, hang it!

indicators.note: the word for paying out is placed all round the abbreviation for America

parts.note: to pay out money is to spend it
US is the usual abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: An exasperated payer has to send money to America and curses the fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hang it!' reads as an oath; 'hang' is the definition and 'it' only completes the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang something up is to dangle it from above, a synonym.

clue.text: Writing up everything is mean

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters for writing are read from bottom to top

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
all means everything

explanation.surface: Writing up the whole story is a petty act.
explanation.definitionFit: Small can mean petty or ungenerous, as mean does.

clue.text: They look for viewers without cunning

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for viewers goes round the word for cunning

parts.note: seers are those who see, viewers
arch means slyly cunning or knowing

explanation.surface: Naive onlookers go searching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside makes SEERS wrap ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Searchers are those who seek, people who look for something.

clue.text: A consumer of some taste — a terse fellow

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: A person of refined taste who speaks curtly.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'tastE A TERse'; 'fellow' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater consumes food, so is one who consumes.

clue.text: This is most unfair!

parts.note: read not as a complaint but as the superlative of the opposite of fair, as light is to dark

explanation.definitionFit: Fair can mean light in colour, so the least fair is the deepest in shade.

clue.text: Split over a cathedral city

parts.note: to rip something is to split or tear it
on means over, as in a lid on (over) a pot

explanation.surface: A city divided over its cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPON is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon in Yorkshire has a cathedral and city status, so it is an example.

clue.text: A letter or card

definitions.meaning: any written symbol of an alphabet
an eccentric or amusing person, as in 'he's a real card'

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a written symbol; the other is an amusing eccentric, as 'card' means in slang.

clue.text: The head's capital investment

definitions.meaning: the head teacher of a school, or chief of an organisation
the sum originally invested, as opposed to the interest earned on it

explanation.surface: A headteacher's money put into a business.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the person in charge of a school; the other is the original sum lent or invested.

clue.text: Caution should be used about opposing cut

indicators.note: the word for caution goes about, that is around, the letter for against

parts.note: care means caution, as in 'take care'
V is short for versus, meaning against or opposing

explanation.surface: Advice to be careful when slicing against the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut, as with a joint of meat or a block of stone: a synonym.

clue.text: Fell back before officer to show respect

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for fell from right to left

parts.note: to fell a tree is to axe it
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed in front of a commander to show deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell back' looks like a retreat; 'back' turns AXE into EXA, which is followed by LT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to praise and honour them highly, a way of showing reverence.

clue.text: Quite ordinary property interests converter

indicators.note: a converter changes things, and here it changes these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A dull estate agent turns property into investments.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being hackneyed or commonplace, a property of something very ordinary.

clue.text: Popular bond — about right for that extra cash!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular, as in 'the in thing'

indicators.note: the word for bond goes about, that is around, the letter for right

parts.note: cement bonds things together

explanation.surface: A popular savings bond pays out a bonus, which is welcome money.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is an addition, especially a regular rise in pay, so extra money.

clue.text: Gloomy forecaster not given credit

parts.note: the Trojan prophetess of Greek myth, cursed so that her true warnings of doom were never believed

explanation.definitionFit: A prophet of doom, after the Trojan seer whose accurate prophecies were disbelieved.

clue.text: Stiff without thinking

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: Rigid and unreflective.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff price is a steep one, so costly.

clue.text: Foodstuffs in test run go off

indicators.note: food that goes off goes bad, and these letters likewise break up into a new order

explanation.surface: Food goes bad during a trial run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' rearranges IN TEST RUN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrients are the nourishing substances in food, so near-synonyms for foodstuffs.

clue.text: A good man in no spirit for quack treatment

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a saint is placed in the phrase no spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit
ST is short for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous man who refuses drink as a fake remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a patent medicine of doubtful worth peddled by a charlatan.

clue.text: The colour is very good in the main

indicators.note: the letters for very good are placed in the word for the main

parts.note: the main is an old poetic name for the sea
pi is short for pious, very good in crossword usage

explanation.surface: A colour that looks great out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) for 'very good' is a crossword convention; 'the main' is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown tint, as seen in old photographs: an example of a colour.

clue.text: A piano harbours such pests

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to harbour a fugitive is to hide them

explanation.surface: Insects shelter inside a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphides, plural of aphis, are greenfly, insect pests of plants.

clue.text: A woman with revolutionary ideas

indicators.note: revolutionary ideas are overturned ones, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A radical woman with subversive thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadie is a female first name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: The repository of Continental cannabis

parts.note: de is French for of, a Continental word
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A store of European marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse, a place where goods are kept.

clue.text: A singer to tease in church

parts.note: to chaff someone is to tease them good-humouredly

explanation.surface: A choirboy is teased during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a songbird, so a bird that sings.

clue.text: The class found overbearing

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it
read as over bearing: in a down clue the word for found sits over E, east, a compass bearing

explanation.surface: The social group was thought domineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overbearing' must be split into over + bearing: CAST goes above E, the compass bearing east.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, as in the Hindu system.

clue.text: "Let's ______ till six, and then have dinner" (Carroll).

definitions.text: "Let's ______ till six, and then have dinner" (Carroll).

parts.words: "Let's ______ till six, and then have dinner" (Carroll).
parts.note: a gap-fill from Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, Tweedledum proposing a battle with his brother

explanation.definitionFit: Tweedledum and Tweedledee agree to do battle, so the missing verb means to do battle.

clue.text: Put down iron in the long grass

indicators.note: the word for iron is placed in the word for the tall grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in water
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Someone is ironing in a field of tall grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress a revolt is to put it down, a synonym.

clue.text: Hard work at the mill?

definitions.meaning: what millstones do to corn, crushing it to flour

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is slogging toil; the other is the crushing action of millstones on grain.

clue.text: Sea-mist obscuring the painter

indicators.note: mist obscures things, and here the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Fog at sea hides an artist from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscuring' rearranges SEA-MIST to give the French painter Henri Matisse.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French artist, so an example of a painter.

clue.text: A number with long hair will take part

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone with flowing locks agrees to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the pieces; 'take part' means play a role on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer takes a part in a play, so one who will play a role.
